prompt:
A photorealistic photograph of a family doctor's examination room in Berlin on a bright morning, in a tall vertical picture. Taken with a 35 mm lens from the middle of the room at seated eye height, looking straight at the examination couch, everything in sharp focus from the floor in the foreground to the back wall. Natural colours, soft daylight from the window.

The two reference pictures show the same young man, from the front and in three-quarter view. His face, hair and build stay exactly as in those pictures; only his clothes change, as written below.

Each object and each person stands on its own, with a band of plain pale-mint wall or light-grey floor around it, so that every one of them can be pointed at separately.

THE PATIENT sits in the middle of the picture on the edge of a padded examination couch covered with a strip of white paper, facing the camera, his whole body in view from the top of his head to his bare feet. He is the man of the reference pictures, with the same face and the same thick dark-brown curly hair; both of his ears show at the sides of his head. His face is turned to the camera, both eyes open, his nose, mouth and chin in full view. He wears a plain light-grey t-shirt with short sleeves and dark-blue track trousers; the right trouser leg is rolled up above the knee, and a small square white plaster sits on his right knee. His two arms hang at his sides with a band of mint wall between each arm and his body, his elbows slightly bent, and his hands rest flat on the white paper a hand's width out from his thighs, the fingers spread. His knees are a little apart, and his bare feet rest on a low grey step in front of the couch with a gap between them, each toe visible. He smiles ruefully at the camera.

THE DOCTOR sits on a low black stool on wheels at the right of the couch, turned towards him, her face in three-quarter view: a woman of about forty with warm brown skin, dark-brown eyes and long black hair tied back in a low bun, in a white doctor's coat over a pale-blue blouse. A black stethoscope hangs around her neck. In both hands, held in front of her at waist height, she has a fresh roll of white elastic bandage. She looks at his knee and smiles kindly.

On the BACK WALL behind the couch, a wide anatomical poster in a thin white frame: a human skeleton seen from the front on a white background, its bones drawn in ivory, with the ribs, the spine and the two lungs clearly drawn in soft colours. Above the poster, a round white wall clock with a black rim, twelve short black tick marks and two black hands showing twenty past nine.

At the LEFT of the picture, a white desk against the wall. On its top: a computer screen showing a plain pale-blue page, a white keyboard in front of it, a white box of tissues with one tissue standing up out of it, a glass of water, a blister pack of white tablets beside a small medicine box, a green health insurance card lying flat, and a blue pen.

At the RIGHT, against the wall behind the doctor, a small steel trolley with two shelves. On the top shelf: a sealed syringe in its clear wrapper, an open box of plasters, and a pair of blue disposable gloves lying flat.

In the back right corner, a tall window with a white frame, showing a sunny sky and the green crown of a tree; on its sill, a green potted plant. In the back left corner, a closed white door with a silver handle, and on a hook beside it a dark-green zipped sports jacket.

On the FLOOR in front of the couch, at the left of the step: a pair of white running shoes side by side, with two white socks laid across them; and a black sports bag with a white-and-black football resting on top of it. A small white pedal bin stands by the desk.

The floor is light-grey vinyl and the walls are pale mint. The room is clean, bright and calm: between the objects and the people, the same plain mint wall and the same grey floor.
